title: LEFT OUTER JOIN

content.intro: This lesson covers left outer join as part of SQLite’s embedded relational database model. Work through one small example, verify the output, and then connect the result to the listed subtopics from the supplied curriculum.

items.title: Preserving unmatched left-side records
items.text: Write an explicit JOIN condition and know the relationship cardinality. A one-to-many join repeats parent rows; aggregate at the intended grain. For LEFT JOINs, a right-table filter in WHERE can remove unmatched left rows.

items.title: NULL values for missing matches
items.text: `NULL` is not zero, false, or empty text. Ordinary equality with NULL is unknown, so use `IS NULL` / `IS NOT NULL` and check how predicates affect rows.

content_blocks.title: Example: LEFT OUTER JOIN
content_blocks.code:
WITH people(id, name) AS (VALUES (1, 'Ari'), (2, 'Bea')), tasks(owner_id, title) AS (VALUES (1, 'Read'))
SELECT people.name, tasks.title FROM people LEFT JOIN tasks ON tasks.owner_id = people.id ORDER BY people.id;
